You hear part of a ward briefing.
 What does the person giving the brief explain is governed by a specific
 law?
A. Who you can share confidential information with and how
B. When and how it is necessary to ask for patient consent
C. When it is more important to give data than protect it

You hear two nurses having a conversation.
 What do the nurses agree about?
A. The value of making patients feel at ease with treatment
B. That nurses spend a lot of their time talking to patients
C. That failures in communication are easily overcome

You hear part of a conversation between a GP and a nurse.
 What issue does the nurse want to address?
A. How patients can confirm their appointments through email
B. How patients can get more out of their consultation time
C. How patients can use videos to know more about their condition
 before their appointment

You hear part of a training on an addiction treatment program.
 Why does the speaker talk about the program?
A. To show the main objective of the initiative
B. To show the type of research being done
C. To show the advances that have been made

You hear part of a conversation between a junior and senior doctor.
 What is the senior doctor explaining to the junior doctor?
A. How the night and day teams share their work load
B. How information about patients is shared within the unit
C. How to the nurse and consultant divide handover duties

You hear part of a conversation between a junior and senior doctor.
 What does the senior doctor point out?
A. Another possible diagnosis for the patient
B. Another area of concern on the X-ray
C. Another possible explanation for the X-ray

According to the interviewee, why is this research needed?
A. To better inform how to treat and diagnose patients
B. To use new methods to do research in medicine
C. To help broaden the number of treatments available

What is the main focus of the interviewee’s research?
A. Using diagnostic systems to predict patient response to
 medication
B. Using new ways of analyzing data to predict patient response to
 medication
C. Using a combination of methods to predict patient response to
 medication

How did previous investigation inform the current research?
A. It brought in learning from fields outside of medicine.
B. It linked brain activity to a person’s reaction to medication.
C. It helped to measure brain activity using resting state
 electroencephalography

In what context was the research conducted?
A. In a small trial with a variety of medications
B. In a large trial with a variety of medications
C. In a large trial with one type of medication

How did the method of analysis compare to other methods?
A. It performed as well as other methods.
B. It performed better than other methods.
C. It performed worse than other methods.

According to the interviewer, what are future implications for this
 method of analysis?
A. It is can be used to predict advanced depression in patients.
B. It can make treatment for depression more personal.
C. It can be used to make treatment better for all patients.

Why does the presenter give statistics about tooth decay?
A. To help the audience understand the scope of the problem
B. To help the audience understand the cost of the problem
C. To help the audience understand possible short-term solutions

Why does the presenter introduce the topic of tooth extractions?
A. Because many people are not aware they take place in a hospital
B. Because it sets the stage for the presenter’s research project
C. Because it helps to explain why the research was undertaken

What kind of intervention was developed for the research project?
A. A planned conversation with parents on prevention strategies
B. A planned program to change bad habits in children’s dental
 health
C. A planned training for dental nurses involved in baby teeth
 extraction

How was the intervention different from the conventional approach?
A. It focused on parental responsibility over their children’s dental
 health.
B. It focused on helping parents set reasonable targets for their
 children’s dental health.
C. It focused on informing parents on how to measure the success of
 their goals related to their children’s dental health.

Did the intervention improve health outcomes?
A. It did not improve health outcomes because children in both
 groups went back to the dentist.
B. It improved health outcomes because children needed less dental
 treatment for cavities.
C. It improved health outcomes because children did not need
 fillings as they had less tooth decay.

According to the speaker, the most important aspect of the intervention
 was…
A. The way it empowered parents to be in charge of their children’s
 dental health.
B. The way it involved trained dental nurses in educating parents
 about their children’s dental health.
C. The way it made dental health care more pleasant for nurses,
 parents and children.
